claims.claim: Saudi Arabia's Supreme Court set aside the death sentence of Anojan Sivarasa, 27, a Sri Lankan migrant worker, over a Facebook comment, according to Colombo's Deputy Foreign Minister Arun Hemachandra.
claims.episode_span: Saudi Arabia's Supreme Court has set aside the death sentence handed to Anojan Sivarasa, 27
claims.source_title: Saudi Arabia overturns death sentence for man over Facebook comment
claims.supporting_quote: Saudi Arabia's Supreme Court has set aside the death sentence handed to a Sri Lankan migrant worker over a comment he made on Facebook, Colombo's Deputy Foreign Minister Arun Hemachandra said.

claims.claim: A Saudi appellate court sentenced Sivarasa to death in September after convicting him of blasphemy against Islam and the Prophet Muhammad.
claims.episode_span: A Saudi appellate court sentenced him to death in September after convicting him of blasphemy
claims.source_title: Saudi Arabia overturns death sentence for man over Facebook comment
claims.supporting_quote: Anojan Sivarasa, 27, was sentenced to death in September after a Saudi appellate court convicted him of blasphemy against Islam and the Prophet Muhammad over his comment.

claims.claim: The Al-Ahsa Criminal Court initially sentenced Sivarasa to five years in prison and a fine of three million Saudi riyals, about 0.8 million dollars.
claims.episode_span: The Al-Ahsa Criminal Court had first sentenced him to five years in prison and a fine of three million Saudi riyals
claims.source_title: Saudi Arabia overturns death sentence for man over Facebook comment
claims.supporting_quote: He was initially sentenced to five years in prison as well as a fine of three million Saudi riyals ($0.8m; £0.6m) by the Al-Ahsa Criminal Court.

claims.claim: Faizer Mustafa confirmed to BBC Sinhala that the death sentence had been overturned and said they are reviewing the Supreme Court's latest ruling.
claims.episode_span: Faizer Mustafa, a Sri Lankan lawmaker involved in the negotiations, confirmed to BBC Sinhala
claims.source_title: Saudi Arabia overturns death sentence for man over Facebook comment
claims.supporting_quote: Faizer Mustafa, a Sri Lankan lawmaker who is involved in legal negotiations with Saudi Arabia regarding Sivarasa's case, confirmed to BBC Sinhala that Saudi Arabia had overturned the death sentence, adding that they are reviewing the Supreme Court's latest ruling.

claims.claim: Sivarasa's family said they have had no direct contact with him since 28 September.
claims.episode_span: his family had said they have had no direct contact with him since 28 September
claims.source_title: Saudi Arabia overturns death sentence for man over Facebook comment
claims.supporting_quote: Sivarasa's family had earlier said they have had no direct contact with him since 28 September.

claims.claim: A record 962,832 candidates are sitting South Africa's 2026 matric exams, which began on 13 October and end on 26 November.
claims.episode_span: A record 962,832 candidates are sitting South Africa's 2026 National Senior Certificate examinations
claims.source_title: From AI tutors to maths clubs, learners find new routes to exam support
claims.supporting_quote: A record 962,832 candidates are sitting for the 2026 National Senior Certificate (NSC) exams, which began on 13 October 2026 and conclude on 26 November 2026.

claims.claim: The exam cohort comprises 815,051 full-time and 147,781 part-time candidates, with about 7,100 centres and more than 51,000 markers.
claims.episode_span: This year's cohort is 815,051 full-time candidates and 147,781 part-time candidates
claims.source_title: From AI tutors to maths clubs, learners find new routes to exam support
claims.supporting_quote: This year’s cohort comprises 815,051 full-time and 147,781 part-time candidates. The Department of Basic Education has established about 7,100 examination centres, and more than 51,000 educators have been recruited to mark scripts.

claims.claim: Residents Francis Jeffrey and Eileen Leander are demanding answers over 2.4 million rand spent on upgrades to Gqeberha's Wylde Bridge after height restrictors were destroyed and heavy trucks continued to cross.
claims.episode_span: demanding to know how 2.4 million rand was spent on upgrades to the historic Wylde Bridge
claims.source_title: ‘Where’d the money go?’ — feisty NMB tannies slam ‘shoddy’ R2.4m Smartie Bridge upgrades
claims.supporting_quote: ‘Feisty tannies’ Francis Jeffrey and Eileen Leander are demanding answers over R2.4m spent on upgrades to Gqeberha’s historic Wylde Bridge, after height restrictors were destroyed and heavy trucks continued to cross the structure, raising safety fears.

claims.claim: Wylde Bridge opened in September 1879, spans the Swartkops River between Amsterdamhoek and Swartkops, and was nicknamed Smartie Bridge after a 2016 refurbishment.
claims.episode_span: It opened in September 1879 and is one of the oldest bridges in the metro.
claims.source_title: ‘Where’d the money go?’ — feisty NMB tannies slam ‘shoddy’ R2.4m Smartie Bridge upgrades
claims.supporting_quote: Spanning the Swartkops River, this historic structure was opened in September 1879, making it one of the oldest bridges in the Nelson Mandela Bay metro. It was nicknamed “Smartie Bridge” after a brightly coloured refurbishment in 2016.

claims.claim: DA councillor Werner Senekal said a motion on the bridge spending was accepted by the Municipal Public Accounts Committee and would be taken further after the 4 November municipal election.
claims.episode_span: the matter will be taken further in the new term, after the municipal election on 4 November
claims.source_title: ‘Where’d the money go?’ — feisty NMB tannies slam ‘shoddy’ R2.4m Smartie Bridge upgrades
claims.supporting_quote: DA Ward 16 councillor Werner Senekal said a motion he submitted seeking clarity on how the money was spent would only be dealt with in detail after the 4 November municipal election.
